discovery.found_by: find_adaptations.py raise verdict that had never entered the mine/classify/traversal pipeline

why_excluded.finding: Born at or above the boundary. Traversal: 'no boundary-crossing bump in the adaptation's ancestry, declared or resolved'.
why_excluded.detail: Raised to Integer.MAX_VALUE. No pom.xml commits found at the repository root, so the module layout differs; traversal resolved the ancestry regardless and found no crossing.
why_excluded.pattern: A `raise` verdict proves the client HIT the limit. It does not prove the client CROSSED the boundary. Five open raise candidates were assessed on 2026-08-16 across two breaks -- mmaudet/eu-dss-module, mkarjun/LCS, havochvatten/MSP-Symphony (jackson 2.15) and OussamaLakhdar90/veritas, AxDevv/FAWE-Folia (snakeyaml 1.32) -- and ALL FIVE were born at or above the boundary. They raised a limit that had been there since the day their project started, because their data outgrew the default. Real adaptations to a constraint; not adaptations to a transition.

traversal_verdict_withdrawn.withdrawn: WITHDRAWN 2026-08-16. This case originally read 'born past the boundary' on the strength of a traversal verdict now known to be unsound: find_boundary_bump returned None both when it had measured no crossing AND when it had measured nothing at all, and verify_traversal rendered None as a confident negative. Re-run against the fixed traversal, this candidate returns UNDECIDED. The born-past claim is withdrawn. See excluded/ineffective_adaptation/jackson-fortnox-reactive-wizard.json for the defect and its regression test.
traversal_verdict_withdrawn.basis: No independent evidence. Re-run returns UNDECIDED: never declared under jackson-core.

revised_basis: The exclusion still stands on a DIFFERENT and now-measured ground: the fixed traversal reports the library was never declared under the break's coordinate in any build file examined -- BOM-managed, or declared under a sibling artifact. Under the direct-only scoping decision that is out of scope. This is a weaker and more contingent basis than born-past; see scoping_caveat.
scoping_caveat: A BOM-managed dependency may not belong with framework-transitive ones. A client that declares com.fasterxml.jackson:jackson-bom and bumps it 2.14.2 -> 2.15.0 is making a deliberate, explicit version choice, and the version IS pinnable via the BOM property -- which is the reason the direct-only rule gave for excluding transitive candidates. That reason does not apply here. If the scoping decision is revisited, this candidate should be reconsidered rather than left excluded by default.
